title: Biomechanical Effects of a Four-Point Frame Knee Brace Under Functional Loads in Chronic Knee Joint Instability
summary: To improve the treatment with braces (orthoses), it is important to perform clinical patient studies. The results of this study should enable doctors and orthopedic technicians to improve the provision of medical aids to patients with unstable knee joints through measurable results. Patients with unstable knee joints following surgical treatment of the anterior cruciate ligament are included in the study if a knee orthosis has been prescribed by their doctors. A biomechanical examination of the knee joint is carried out during a one-time appointment, during which the patient must perform simple jumps and changes of direction in addition to walking. Additionally, a questionnaire will be used to assess the comfort of the brace.
conditions: chronic instability of the knee joint: crucial ligament anterior

interventions.name:
Prospective, non-interventional study
25 patients after surgical treatment of ACL ruptures with existing clinical anterior instability of the knee joint ≥ 3 months and indication for revision  surgery who were treated with a partially flexible knee joint orthosis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• treated ACL ruptures with existing clinical anterior instability of the knee joint ≥ 3 months and indication for revision surgery
•knee laxity: side difference in the Lachmann-test using Rolimeter of ≥ 4mm
• physically active (Tegner Score ≥4)
• healthy contralateral side
• side difference in the single leg hop of ≥ 10%
• indication for prescription of a functional knee brace
Exclusion criteria:
• injuries of the PCL
• medial instability > Grad I according to Hughston
